scan_shows: The three decreasing strokes are all visible. The middle line has an independent short down-left return at its right end. The upper line rises slightly toward its right tip; these physical details are reproduced.; crops/168_10_divider.jpg [626, 1084, 1080, 1193]

The opening marks are two raised upright strokes; the closing marks have two raised ends connected by a shallow curve. Neither pair consists of guillemet chevrons.; crops/168_12_typequotes.jpg [739, 1409, 1377, 1514]

The final separated low strokes fit r and a flattened e-exit; no independent s is secure. The plural remains possible in the compressed terminal run, so record genres as a doubt without changing the preferred genre or counts.; crops/168_17_tous_genre.jpg [1061, 1948, 1449, 2059]

The sign above the last i has one short oblique stroke. No distinct second arm establishes a circumflex, although a compressed circumflex remains possible; the unaccented form stays first and marked.; crops/168_18_disparait.jpg [808, 2248, 1141, 2343]

A separate dark curved stroke descends below the end of the word at the right edge. Its visible upper curve and falling lower end identify a comma despite the tip reaching the paper edge.; crops/168_19_virtuellement.jpg [1169, 2253, 1613, 2364]

A smaller detached dark point appears lower and farther right than the clear full stop. It may be incidental ink, so it is retained as a doubtful extra point rather than assigned a new punctuation function.; crops/second/168_B21.jpg [409, 966, 710, 1083]
Two detached raised strokes precede catégorie; neither is an angular guillemet.; crops/169_cat_open.jpg [414, 115, 689, 207]
Two short raised strokes follow the final e of homotopique, before the opening parenthesis.; crops/169_cat_close.jpg [688, 111, 1137, 208]

The word has a tall b ascender and lower bowl, a short r shoulder, a separate dot over i, and a low n with a short terminal descent. There is no separate s after n. The following de zinc is fully visible.; crops/169_brin_zinc.jpg [1001, 281, 1520, 372]
After the final e-shaped turn there is a prolonged low terminal stroke that can carry a reduced s. The stroke does not settle plural against singular.; crops/169_cohomologies.jpg [504, 553, 871, 648]

line: L7: coefficient ending and possible accent
scan_shows: The final t has a tall upright, detached crossbar and low foot with no following s. A separate compact dark mark directly over the first e precedes both tall f strokes; unlike the later i dots it has no i stem beneath it. It may be a point-like accent, so coéfficient is preferred literally with coefficient retained if the mark is incidental. The singular ending remains resolved.; crops/169_coefficient.jpg [975, 549, 1338, 649]
The word ends in the tall crossed t and its exit stroke. No independent final s is present.; crops/169_constant_tordus.jpg [841, 646, 1143, 737]
Two raised, separately inked curved ticks precede the q; they are not a guillemet.; crops/169_question_open.jpg [506, 826, 712, 924]
Two raised short strokes follow X; the second curves downward.; crops/169_question_close.jpg [167, 913, 276, 987]

The first underline ends below c, to the left of the detached abbreviation stop. A second, separate underline runs under constants. The stop is outside the first underline.; crops/169_loc_underline.jpg [177, 1003, 632, 1094]

line: L12: inline map and overlapping f
scan_shows: The tall f crosses the connecting shaft near its right end; its own short crossbar is higher. The shaft has only a small thickening beyond f, not an unequivocal separate arrowhead. X and the raised prime of X′ are clear. Standard math preserves the first C reading without drawing running text.; crops/169_inline_map.jpg [995, 974, 1228, 1081]

The terminal t has a high upright, a detached crossbar, and a low exit. No independent final s follows, unlike the distinct s in the underlined constants above.; crops/169_constant_second.jpg [335, 1301, 626, 1389]

A single compact dot stands over the i; no two-sided circumflex is visible. The tall vertical overlapping h descends from the q in the preceding line. The insertion guide attaches de chaines before abéliens.; crops/169_chaines_insert.jpg [1219, 1328, 1569, 1487]
After the looped l, compressed on, and descending g, a separate stop is visible. No u, e, u, or r follows before n.; crops/169_long_insert.jpg [170, 1477, 565, 1611]

line: L17: placement of de long. n
scan_shows: The words are above the running baseline. A long guide curves down at the left and attaches them immediately before à faisceaux, after abéliens.; crops/169_long_insert.jpg [170, 1477, 565, 1611]

The cancellation crosses a clear looped l and lower a, then compressed bodies and a tall t, with low i/o/n-like strokes at the end. These support la notion, but the crossing obscures the full ending enough to retain the longer alternative. The added ce is above the same phrase.; crops/169_notion_ce.jpg [441, 1702, 706, 1802]
A low oval and looped d ascender are followed by a connected low e/exit; the raised opening tick of the added word is spatially separate.; crops/169_de_objets.jpg [983, 1691, 1293, 1801]

The heavy horizontal begins under O and continues beneath the added word. No separate lower letter bodies form another cancelled word; the crossing vertical is the descender of j.; crops/169_de_objets.jpg [983, 1691, 1293, 1801]

The opening O is a large angular rounded form of nearly the height of the following b, followed by a descending j, small e, tall crossed t and compressed s. It is unlike the low oval o elsewhere on this page.; crops/169_de_objets.jpg [983, 1691, 1293, 1801]

line: L19 insertion: quotation marks around Objets
scan_shows: One tall detached tick is visible to the left of O. At the right, a hooked double bend joins the end of the underline; no independent pair of raised ticks can be isolated. Single marks remain the preferred reading, with double marks and absence of a separate closing mark retained. H marks the letters of objets uncertain but does not transcribe the quotation marks.; crops/169_de_objets.jpg [983, 1691, 1293, 1801]

line: L19 insertion: underline extent of Objets
scan_shows: The heavy underline starts under O, well to the right of the detached opening tick, and runs beneath the letters to a hooked end. It does not begin under the opening quotation mark.; crops/169_de_objets.jpg [983, 1691, 1293, 1801]
The final looped l returns to the baseline before the closing parenthesis. The intervening space has no detached period.; crops/169_diagram_top.jpg [605, 1882, 1169, 2057]

line: Diagram top: double underline under modulo
scan_shows: Two separate parallel horizontal strokes lie below modulo. H’s body uses one emphasis wrapper; its editorial note separately acknowledges the double underline. The possible accent remains doubtful.; crops/169_diagram_top.jpg [605, 1882, 1169, 2057]

A single long stroke lies beneath homotopie, beginning after n-. H’s diagram body leaves the word plain, although its editorial note mentions the underline.; crops/169_diagram_top.jpg [605, 1882, 1169, 2057]

A tall p-like stem, a very short shoulder/possible r, and a weak detached stop survive. There are no clearly separable è and s bodies. The full près in the opposite node explains the phrase but cannot supply those letters here.; crops/169_diagram_left.jpg [245, 2224, 634, 2353]

The opening pair meets in a small V-shaped pair of ticks above the s; the closing pair is two separate raised short strokes. They are not guillemets.; crops/169_diagram_right.jpg [976, 2217, 1542, 2350]

line: Diagram lower right: separator after n
scan_shows: Two small separated low marks follow n, with pale space between them. They may be the surviving ends of a weak hyphen, so the C alternatives remain.; crops/169_diagram_right.jpg [976, 2217, 1542, 2350]
